To introduce undergraduate and postgraduate courses for all engineering branches and award of Ph.D degree to be one of the best engineering colleges in the country and to be a deemed university.

We strive to provide and maintain academic environment and systems, enabling maximum learning to produce competent professionals. We also aim at achieving this through transparent academic and administrative policies in the college. We intend to provide conducive atmosphere for research, development and consultancy services to our faculty at national and international level.

title: Director

text:
Section: Director
Dr. Hemant Ahuja, the esteemed Director of Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, Ghaziabad, is a seasoned professional with an illustrious career spanning over 22 years in academia and industry.
title: Director

text:
Section: Director
Graduating with honors in Electrical Engineering from Kurukshetra University in 2001, Dr. Ahuja’s journey continued with an M.Tech. in Energy and Environmental Management from the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi, in 2008. His exceptional academic prowess was recognized with the Prof. O.P. Gupta Gold Medal, an accolade bestowed upon him for achieving the highest CGPA during his M.Tech. program. Dr. Ahuja’s academic pursuits culminated in a PhD from IIT Delhi in 2013, cementing his reputation as a dedicated scholar.
title: Director

text:
Section: Director
His expertise lies in the domains of Electrical Machines, Power Electronics, and Wind Energy Conversion Systems. Dr. Ahuja’s scholarly contributions extend across more than 50 publications in prestigious international journals and conferences. His commitment to innovation is evident in his patent achievements, with several patents published under his name. Notably, he has successfully led two research projects funded under TEQIP-III, underscoring his proactive engagement in advancing knowledge.
title: Director

text:
Section: Director
As a valued member of influential professional bodies such as IEEE, PES, ISTE, and IEI, Dr. Ahuja actively contributes to the growth and development of his field. His collaboration with the IEI-Ghaziabad local center as an eminent engineer reflects his dedication to community-driven initiatives. Moreover, Dr. Ahuja plays a pivotal role in shaping Electrical Engineering activities at the Abdul Kalam Technical University level, serving as a member of the Board of Studies for Electrical Engineering at AKTU.
title: Director

text:
Section: Director
Dr. Hemant Ahuja’s multifaceted expertise, dedication to academia, and active involvement in research and collaboration position him as a visionary leader at the helm of Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, driving excellence and innovation in engineering education.
title: Director

Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
The AKGEC Library System comprises of a Central Library, nine Departmental Libraries and five Hostel Libraries.
title: Library

text:
Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
The Central Library, housed in the Administrative Block of the College, consists of two sections spread over 1465 sq. m and with a seating capacity for 344 users. Comfortable study space is provided for faculty, staff and students in the form of reading hall, study cubicles, digital library and faculty reading room.
title: Library

text:
Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
The state-of-the-art facilities include KOHA Open Source Library Management Software, Web Based Online Public Access Catalogue (Web OPAC), Digital Library, DSpace Institutional Repository Server and Membership to DELNET and National Digital Library.
title: Library

text:
Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
The library system is very user friendly with sufficient resources to meet the requirements of the users. Addition of resources as per the requirements and norms is a regular feature. Sufficient number of qualified staff are employed to manage the activities of the library.
title: Library

text:
Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
The Departmental and Hostel libraries are managed and run by the respective departments and hostels with resources on loan from the Central Library.
title: Library

text:
Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
All students, faculty and staff of the College are entitled to make use of the library facilities on availing library membership.
title: Library

text:
Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
Admission to the Central Library is through Library cum Identity Card, which is scanned at the entrance, to keep record of the users. The library is under camera surveillance through ten cameras that have been installed at various locations.
title: Library

text:
Section: Library
Heading: About AKGEC Central Library
The library attracts an average of 350 users on a regular working day.

The six campus hostels are spread over four complexes namely, the Junior Girls Hostel Complex, the Girls Hostel Complex, the Junior Boys Hostel Complex and the Senior Boys Hostel Complex. The three girls hostel have double and triple seater rooms and accommodate about 600 students. The Junior Boys Hostel having double occupancy rooms can accommodate about 300 students and is reserved for first year students. The Senior Boys Hostel Complex has two hostels with single and triple seater accommodation and houses about 600 students.

Hostels are equipped with eco-friendly solar water heating systems. Hostels also have canteens and provision stores for minor item of daily requirement. The hostels thus provide reasonable levels of comfort, hygienic food, recreation facilities and an environment conducive for pursuit of academic and all round development.

Civil Engineering is the art of directing the sources of power in nature for the use and convenience of man, for improvement of quality of life. The theory and practice of Civil Engineering is basically applied in the construction of buildings & structures, roads, bridges, aqueducts, canals, river navigation ports, docks and harbours.At AKGEC, B.Tech course in Civil Engineering is offered with intake capacity of 60.The goal of the department is to produce high quality technical manpower needed by industry, R&D organizations and academic institutions and above all to meet the engineering needs of the nation.The faculty comprises of galaxies of qualified and experienced teachers with Ph.D and M Tech from premier institutions like IITs and NITs.

Section: Computer Science and Engineering
Heading: HOD
Dr. Anu Chaudhary, is a Professor and Head at the Department of Computer Science and Engineering. He has an extensive background in both academia and industry, with over 22 years of experience. He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Gurukul Kangari University, Hardwar (U.K) India, specializing in the field of “Performance Evaluation of High Speed Data Networks." He also has an M. Tech in Computer Science from Birla Institute of Technology (BIT), Mesra Ranchi, and an MCA from the University of Madras. Dr. Chaudhary has made notable contributions to research, having published more than 20 research papers in both international and national journals and conferences. He holds 6 patents at the national level. His academic engagement includes guiding Ph.D. scholars, as well as supervising numerous M.Tech, MCA, and B.Tech projects. Dr. Chaudhary current area of research is in the field of High Speed Data Networks, Machine Learning, Data Science and related domains.
title: Computer Science and Engineering

text:
Section: Computer Science and Engineering
Heading: HOD
He's an active participant in the academic community, serving on editorial and reviewer boards of various national and international journals. He has also taken on leadership roles by chairing multiple national and international conferences. Dr. Chaudhary is a member of several technical societies, including the Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (IETE) and the Computer Society of India (CSI).

text:
Section: Electronics and Communication Engineering
The Electronics and Communication stream represents two fastest growing technology areas in view of exponential growth taking place in our country. Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) involves researching, designing, developing and testing of electronic equipment used in various systems. Electronics and Communication Engineering is also considered as the backbone of the modern communication system. In the current scenario, modern applications like the Internet of Things (IoT), Robotics, and Embedded Systems are highly dependent on the knowledge of ECE. Electronics and Communications engineers also conceptualize and oversee the manufacturing of communications and broadcast systems. It has an important role from defence sector to space programs to the basic need of human beings including the internet to the entertainment industry. Electronics and Communication Engineering has a wide scope as compared to other.
title: Electronics and Communication Engineering

text:
Section: Electronics and Communication Engineering
There are numerous opportunities to build a career after completing the engineering course in the field of Electronics and Communication Engineering. An individual can make his/her career in IT industry, defence, telecommunications, electronic and hardware manufacturing, embedded systems development, software development, power sector, TV and music industry, automobiles, space communications, home appliances development, electronic security systems, mobile phones testing and development, communication protocols development and optical communications development among others.
title: Electronics and Communication Engineering

Prof. (Dr.) Neelesh Kumar Gupta is a seasoned professional with an illustrious career spanning over 22 years of teaching in reputed technical institutes. He obtained Ph.D in Electronics and Communication Engineering from Rajiv Gandhi Technical University (RGTU), Bhopal (M.P.). Presently, Dr. Neelesh Kumar Gupta is working as Professor & HoD in Electronics and Communication Engineering Department & IQAC Coordinator at Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, Ghaziabad (U.P.)-India. Earlier he served in TRUBA Institute of Engineering and Information Technology, Bhopal as Prof. & HoD ECE. He completed his Graduation (B.E.) in Electronics and Communication Engineering from Rajiv Gandhi Prodhyogiki Vishwavidyalaya (RGPV), Bhopal (M.P.) in 2002 and his Post-Graduation (M. Tech) from the prestigious Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology (MANIT), Bhopal (M.P.) in 2007 with specialization in “Microwave and Millimeter Waves”.
title: Electronics and Communication Engineering

Electrical Engineering stream involve the study and applications of Electricity, Electronics and Electromagnetics that entails and encompasses Power Engineering, Control Systems, Signal Processing, Digital Computers and Instrumentation. Section: Electrical and Electronics Engineering
Heading: HOD
Dr. Lokesh Varshney is a Professor and the Head of the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering. He has over 18 years of rich and extensive experience in academics and research. He received his B.E. degree in Electrical Engineering from SGSITS, Indore, in 2004. He earned his M.Tech. and Ph.D. in Electrical Machines and Drives from the Indian Institute of Technology, Banaras Hindu University, in 2009 and 2014, respectively. His areas of expertise include Electrical Machines, Power Electronics, Network Analysis Systems, and Renewable Energy Systems. He has over 66 publications in various international journals, conferences, and book chapters. He has eight patents filed and twelve patents published. Dr. Varshney is a member of several professional bodies. Four research scholars have been awarded Ph.D. degrees under his guidance, one has submitted their thesis, and three are ongoing. Seventeen postgraduate thesis have been completed under his guidance. Dr. Varshney is a reviewer for several journals (SCI/WOS).

Section: Mechanical Engineering
Department of Mechanical Engineering at AKGEC was formed in 1998 with inception of the college. The Department provides an outstanding research environment complemented by excellence in teaching. Ever since its inception, the department has been a pioneering academic centre for higher education, research, and innovation in key areas of Mechanical Engineering. The department provides full support to MTech. scholars in terms dissertation guidance, lab facilities and access to international and national journals. Experienced and senior faculty members are assigned for MTech courses and dissertation work of the scholars. The faculty members and M Tech scholars have published good quality research papers in peer-reviewed and indexed journals and International Conferences.

Heading: HOD
Dr. Devendra Singh is the Professor and Head of the Department of Mechanical Engineering. He completed his B.Tech. in Mechanical Engineering from Motilal Nehru Regional Engineering College, Allahabad (presently MNNIT, Allahabad) in 1992. He served in various industries and then began his teaching career as a faculty member at Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College in September 2000. He completed his M.Tech. in Automation and Robotics in 2009 and was awarded a Ph.D. in Machine Design in 2017 from the Department of Mechanical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Jamia Millia Islamia University, New Delhi.
title: Mechanical Engineering

text:
Section: Mechanical Engineering
Heading: HOD
His areas of expertise include Mechanical Design, Robotics, and Materials Engineering. He was awarded by the Vice-Chancellor of UPTU for excellence in teaching Machine Design and Engineering Mechanics. He also secured third position in India in the NPTEL examination in Engineering Mechanics. His prime focus is on promoting academic research and innovation among the faculty and students of the Department of Mechanical Engineering.

Section: Master of Computer Applications
MCA strives for excellence and has been consistently maintaining excellent academic results and placements. It is a matter of pride for the department to maintain a superlative overall academic performance over the years. MCA achieved 1st position in the University merit list in 2022-23. In the year 2018-19, MCA achieved seventh position in the University merit list. The department achieved unbeatable distinction of 6 positions with Gold and Bronze medals in the year 2017-18. Two positions were bagged in 2016-17 and 2015-16 each, three positions with Gold medal 2014-15 and similar stupendous results in previous years as well.

The laboratories have sufficient latest computers and relevant licensed software. State-of-the-art computing facilities networked through broadband are available for Internet access. The department has a fully automated central library equipped with text and reference books, national/international journals including e-journals and multimedia resources.

Section: Master of Computer Applications
Heading: HOD
Prof. (Dr.) Saroj Bala is working as the Professor and Head of the Department of Master of Computer Applications. She has been associated with the department since 23 July 2007. She has an extensive experience of 26 years in teaching and research. She has completed her Ph.D. from Shobhit University, Meerut, MCA from Punjabi University, Patiala, and B.Sc. (CS) from Kurukshetra University, Kurukshetra. She has done NPTEL domain certification in Artificial Intelligence.
title: Master of Computer Applications

text:
Section: Master of Computer Applications
Heading: HOD
Her research interests include artificial intelligence, swarm intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, cyber security, and image processing. She has attended and organized several seminars, workshops, and conferences. She has published 11 research papers in reputed international conferences and journals. She has also published 9 patents including 2 design patents. She has supervised more than 50 MCA projects. Her current research work includes cyber security, medical image processing and large language models.

text:
Section: Conatus
Heading: Activities of Conatus : (2022-23)
Team Conatus hosted a prestigious two-day field event titled “Ronins of Citadel" tailored specifically for 1st and 2nd-year students. The event was held on the 12th and 17th of May 2023, commencing from 4:00 PM to 6:15 PM on both days. The initial day's activities unfolded within the college campus, while the following day's events took place in the well-equipped labs of the CS/IT Block.
title: Conatus

text:
Section: Conatus
Heading: Activities of Conatus : (2022-23)
Registration for the event commenced on the 10th of May 2023, attracting an overwhelming response with more than 150 teams enthusiastically enrolling to participate. Each team comprised three adept members, creating a competitive and engaging atmosphere throughout the event.
title: Conatus

text:
Section: Conatus
Heading: Activities of Conatus : (2022-23)
The competition structure was designed to consist of two distinct rounds, each aimed at assessing different facets of the participants' skills and abilities. The first day featured the captivating game round, wherein teams undertook a series of challenging tasks that expertly tested both their mental acumen and physical prowess. These tasks were strategically placed in various zones dispersed across the campus, ensuring an exhilarating and dynamic experience for the participants.
title: Conatus

text:
Section: Conatus
Heading: Activities of Conatus : (2022-23)
On the second day, the focus shifted to the technical round, an intellectually stimulating segment of the event. Shortlisted teams were presented with encrypted statements, and it was their coding expertise that came into play as they endeavored to decipher these cryptic challenges. The teams earned points based on their successful decryption of the statements, contributing to their overall standing in the competition.
title: Conatus

text:
Section: Conatus
Heading: Activities of Conatus : (2022-23)
Following the completion of both rounds, a comprehensive evaluation process was conducted, wherein the scores from each round were meticulously combined. The final results were then calculated based on this comprehensive assessment, determining the standout participants and ultimately, the victors of the “Ronins of Citadel" event.
title: Conatus

Section: Oorja
Heading: Introduction
KSHITIJ — THE DAWN OF POSSIBILITIES (One-Day Workshop on Sensors, NI LabVIEW, PLC and Embedded Systems)
title: Oorja

text:
Section: Oorja
Heading: Introduction
Kshitij – The Dawn of Possibilities was a one-day workshop held on on 25 August 2026 in CS-IT Seminar Hall, organised by Team Oorja, the technical society of the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, AKGEC. The workshop was designed to give participants a single-day, end-to-end view of how modern industrial and embedded systems are built — beginning with how sensors capture the physical world, moving through NI LabVIEW as a graphical measurement and control platform, into the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) as the backbone of industrial automation, and finally into embedded systems that tie sensing, computation and connectivity together.
title: Oorja

text:
Section: Oorja
Heading: Introduction
The inaugural address was marked by the presence of esteemed faculty members of the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering and our society faculty incharge M/s Nupur Mittal along with the Head of Department Dr. Lokesh Varshney, whose encouragement set an enthusiastic tone for the day ahead.
title: Oorja

text:
Section: Oorja
Heading: Introduction
Session 1 — Sensors: The Eyes and Ears of Modern Technology The day opened with a session on sensors, led by team members Manish and Chirag. The session introduced sensors as the bridge between the physical world and electronic control, following the core engineering pattern of physical quantity → sensor → signal → controller → action. Participants were walked through everyday sensing devices such as the DHT11 temperature-and-humidity module and the PIR motion sensor, followed by soil-moisture and photoelectric sensors used in irrigation and industrial inspection.
title: Oorja

text:
Section: Oorja
Heading: Introduction
Session 2 — NI LabVIEW: From Graphical Programming to Real-World Systems Engineering The second session was led by the team of Priyanshi, Saanvi, Himanshu and Aniket, and introduced participants to National Instruments LabVIEW as a graphical programming and systems-engineering platform used for test, measurement, data acquisition, hardware control and automation. Starting from an engineering problem of testing an electric motor, the speakers explained the concept of a Virtual Instrument (VI) — combining a front panel, block diagram, and icon/connector pane — and how a computer with LabVIEW and appropriate hardware becomes a customised instrument in its own right.
title: Oorja

text:
Section: Oorja
Heading: Introduction
Session 3 — PLC: The Programmable Logic Controller The third session, conducted by the team of Swapnil, Arjun and Tanmay, took participants through the evolution and working of the Programmable Logic Controller. The session began by placing automation in everyday context before tracing its history from manual control and pneumatic systems through hardwired relay logic to modern, software-based, reprogrammable PLCs — illustrated with a live example of a relay-based star-delta starter panel and the wiring complexity it once demanded.
title: Oorja

text:
Section: Oorja
Heading: Introduction
Session 4 — Embedded Systems The concluding technical session was led by the team of Akshara, Akshita, Nikhil and Gaurav, and focused on embedded systems, covering the basics of Arduino and ESP32 as platforms where sensing, computation and connectivity converge. Building on the concepts introduced earlier in the day, the session covered the working of microcontrollers, their programming, and how embedded platforms integrate sensors and communication modules to build complete, responsive systems. Participants were introduced to the basics of Arduino programming, including simple LED blinking and push-button interfacing activities. The session also covered the basics of ESP32, its Wi-Fi connectivity, and basic programming through an LED blinking example. These activities gave participants a practical understanding of how sensing, control logic, programming and connectivity come together inside an embedded device to sense, decide and act in real time.
title: Oorja

Heading: 20 September 2025
Team Phoenix celebrated its 20th Founder’s Day on 20 September 2025 with enthusiasm and technical spirit by setting up a technical board near the Back Block as part of its annual tradition. After the installation, formal invitations were extended to faculty members, and third-year students of Team Phoenix explained the theme and working of the board to faculty and interested students. The board was based on the theme “Waves & Wonders: Unlocking the Power of Communication Systems,” visually representing modern communication technologies such as radio waves, fiber optics, satellite communication, and IoT networks. A Smart Medicine Dispenser System was demonstrated, using an ESP32 controller, RFID-based authentication, and servo motors for secure and automated medicine dispensing, with provision for future IoT and cloud integration.

Heading: Robocon 2020- (Rank -Air 15)
ABU Robocon 2020 was originally scheduled to be hosted in Suva, Fiji and the game will be based on Fiji's national sport rugby. The theme is “ROBO RUGBY 7s", in this game, each team designs two robots, one as a pass robot, and another as a try robot. Each can either be manual or automated. The pass robot will pick up the rugby balls, and the try robot needs to either place them to the trying spot, or to kick the ball passing through a pole. Team scores points depending on the step and the zone location, but points can be awarded to the opponent's team if the kicking ball lands on the opponent's zone. The game ends when three minutes have passed, or when all seven kicking balls (shared for both teams) have been kicked.

The Indian Society for Technical Education (ISTE) is a national, professional, non-profit making Society registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860. It was first started in 1941 as the Association of Principals of Technical Institutions (APTI) and converted into “Indian Society for Technical Education" in 1968 with a view to enlarge its activities to advance the cause of technological education.The major objective of ISTE is to assist and contribute in the production and development of top quality professional engineers and technicians needed by the industries and other organisations.

SAE AKGEC successfully organized Aacar 9.0, an automotive workshop held on May 18-19, 2024. Attendees also gained valuable hands-on experience in one of the best-equipped labs, thanks to our collaboration with BOSCH Lab (JCC and EBCS).

Heading: WORKSHOPS
The SAE Collegiate Club AKGEC organized the AACAR 8.0 workshop on 13th and 14th May 2023, with the primary aim of fostering awareness about automobiles among junior participants. The event, held in the Main Seminar Hall, focused on providing participants with comprehensive theoretical knowledge about automobile components and systems, supplemented by practical demonstrations. With SAE's commitment to engineering innovation, the workshop aimed to bridge the gap between theoretical learning and practical application.
title: SAE India

text:
Section: SAE India
Heading: WORKSHOPS
Over the two-day workshop, participants were immersed in a rich learning experience. Theory sessions covering chassis, brakes, transmission systems, engine, suspension, steering and electronic system. Practical demonstrations included the disassembly and reassembly of Maruti's K12MN engine, showcasing the inner workings of the engine, featuring demonstrations of Ambassador's gearbox overhaul, braking system functionality, and chassis concepts using a Swift Dzire, along with presentations on power steering and electronic components. The event concluded with a quiz competition and introductions of mentors and coordinators, fostering a holistic learning experience.
title: SAE India

text:
Section: SAE India
Heading: WORKSHOPS
In conclusion, the AACAR 8.0 workshop successfully delivered a comprehensive understanding of automobile systems through theoretical sessions and hands-on demonstrations. The event not only deepened participants' knowledge but also inspired them to think innovatively and practically, aligning perfectly with SAE – AKGEC's commitment to promoting engineering creativity and application.

title: College Awards

text:
Section: College Awards
Heading: Accreditation of Measurement and Metrology Centre by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL)
Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, in its endeavor to impart engineering education commensurate with the requirements of Industries, have established a world class Measurement & Metrology Centre in collaboration with Zeiss. It is equipped with 3D Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM), Surface Roughness Testing, Contour Measurement and 3D Scanning setup, along with the regular measuring instruments and accessories. The facility has now been accredited by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) as per ISO / IEC 17025:2017 standard, complying with “General Requirements for the Competence of Testing & Calibration Laboratories.”
title: College Awards

text:
Section: College Awards
Heading: Accreditation of Measurement and Metrology Centre by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL)
National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), aconstituent Board of Quality Council of India has been established with the objective of providing Government, Industry Associations and Industry in general with a scheme of Conformity Assessment Body’s accreditation which involves third-party assessment of the technical competence of testing including medical and calibration laboratories, proficiency testing providers and reference material producers. It is a full member (MRA signatory) to International Laboratory Accreditation Co-operation (ILAC) as well as Asia Pacific Laboratory Accreditation Co-operation (APLAC) since 2000 on the basis of peer evaluation by APLAC as per ISO/IEC 17011:2004.
title: College Awards

Heading: Accreditation of Measurement and Metrology Centre by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL)

With this recognition, the measurement and metrology centre at AKGEC joins one of the very few elite laboratories setup by an Engineering Institute,to be accredited by NABL in the country. The centre now looks forward to offer the services in Dimension Metrology to the nearby Industries and Research Organizations.

text:
Section: T&P Programmes
Heading: PROGRAMMES FOR STUDENTS
Academic excellence alone is not enough and cannot guarantee a good career. Certain personality attributes and soft skills are essential not only to get a good job but also to be able to contribute and grow in an organization. Taking cognizance of this, the college emphasises all round development through a range of extracurricular activities as well as organizing and conducting formal Personality Development Program.
title: T&P Programmes

text:
Section: T&P Programmes
Heading: PROGRAMMES FOR STUDENTS
This programme spanning over 100 hours is conducted by a professional agency and includes training in communication skills, group discussion, interpersonal skills and interviews. This is a mandatory programme for second year B.Tech. and MCA students of the college. This programme helps in the overall personality development of students. The whole exercise is intended to increase the employability of students. Amidst an inspiring and invigorating environment, students undergo training that turns them into top notch professionals.

Section: T&P Programmes
Heading: PROGRAMMES FOR STUDENTS
As a step towards grooming students into perfect professionals and to make them compatible with the IT industry, Infosys campus connect programme (Springboard) is run by T&P department which is conducted by Infosys. Under this programme, Infosys train some identified faculty on emerging courses under Faculty Enabled Program (FEP). In this program B. Tech III year CSE, IT students undergo training on emerging certification courses by Infosys on Springboard platform under the guidance of trained faculty.

text:
Section: About VE Cell
Heading: VISION
To become an International resource Center dedicated to spreading the ethos of value education, fostering individual and societal transformation towards achieving just and equitable society.
title: About VE Cell

text:
Section: About VE Cell
Heading: MISSION
The mission of the Value Education Cell is to foster an environment that promotes value education, and value-based living within the college community. It aims to inspire research into holistic designs, models, systems, and technologies that support these values. Additionally, the cell is committed to assisting in the development of value-based policies, ensuring that the principles of ethical and responsible living are embedded in the institutional framework and practices.
title: About VE Cell

text:
Section: About VE Cell
Heading: MISSION
As the twenty-first century unfolds, technological advancements are becoming more evident. Though, on the one hand, the technologies have made our living more comfortable, on the other, it has caused problems at the level of individuals, family , society and the nature at large in the form of stress/strain, psychosomatic diseases, family break-ups, terrorism, wars, anti-people ecology, resource depletion etc. Technological progress has made the degradation of values and ethical conduct evident. It shows that advancements in technology only cannot lead to a happy, prosperous & meaningful life for a human being. Thus, there is a need to progress in developing technologies (learning skills) and inculcate human values, ensuring complementarity between the two. The complementarity will ensure the holistic utilization of technological systems with a holistic worldview gained through value education. A holistic worldview would then ensure one’s living in harmony with family, society, and Nature/Existence and help us move towards excellence in all spheres.
title: About VE Cell

text:
Section: About VE Cell
Heading: MISSION
To ensure an eco-friendly environment, healthy work culture and to develop a holistic worldview among faculty members, students, staff, and their family members as well as nearby areas, Value Education Cell (VE Cell) was established in AKGEC during the year 2017 under the guidelines of AKTU with the following objectives:
title: About VE Cell

text:
Section: About VE Cell
Heading: MISSION
• Develop right understanding by sharing the understanding of what to do (Value Education). • Develop right skills by teaching how to do (Technical Education). • Practice right living during the period of education and its continuity. • Living in relationship with other human beings leading to mutual happiness. • Living in relationships with rest-of-nature leading to mutual prosperity and hence ensuring an eco-friendly environment in the campus.
title: About VE Cell

text:
Section: About VE Cell
Heading: MISSION
In June 2019, AKGEC was upgraded to a Regional Nodal Center. The underlying principle was that besides conducting of Human Value programs in their own institute, a larger number of teachers from surrounding Colleges/Institutes could also attend programs/workshops and become resource persons for the further spread of Human Values education. The journey, so far, has been very satisfying and fulfilling for all. The College has now been recognized as an active nerve center of Value Education by AICTE where faculty members are voluntarily working to spread this education at various levels across the country.
title: About VE Cell

Section: Transformative Sharing
The Value Education (VE) Cell in the college is dedicated to promoting holistic education that focuses on personal transformation and the cultivation of values such as empathy, compassion, and integrity. The VE Cell’s efforts have yielded significant results, as many faculty members have reported experiencing personal transformations that have led to qualitative changes in their teaching practices and interpersonal relationships.
title: Transformative Sharing

text:
Section: Transformative Sharing
Several faculty members have reported that their teaching has improved as a result of the VE Cell’s emphasis on values-based education. They have become more aware of their communication style, developed a deeper understanding of their student’s needs and learning styles, and created more engaging learning experiences for their students. These faculty members have also developed a greater sense of empathy and compassion for their students, which has helped to build stronger and more positive relationships.
title: Transformative Sharing

text:
Section: Transformative Sharing
The personal transformations experienced by faculty members have not been limited to their professional lives. Many have reported feeling more fulfilled and purposeful in their work, and have developed a greater sense of meaning and direction in their lives. This has led to a deeper connection with their surrounding and a commitment to making a positive difference in the lives of others.
title: Transformative Sharing

text:
Section: Transformative Sharing
The efforts of the Value Education (VE) Cell have impacted not only the faculty members but also the students. The students have been exposed to the Universal Human Values (UHV) contents as part of the curriculum and the evening workshops. As a result, many have reported experiencing personal transformations.
title: Transformative Sharing

text:
Section: Transformative Sharing
According to some students, the UHV contents have helped them to develop a greater sense of responsibility towards their bodies, families, societies, and the environment. They have reported feeling more connected to their surroundings and have become more aware of the impact of their actions on the world around them. They have developed a sense of accountability towards their own well-being and the well-being of others.
title: Transformative Sharing

text:
Section: Transformative Sharing
Moreover, the students have also reported experiencing positive changes in their behavior and attitudes. They have become more respectful towards their teachers and colleagues, and have developed a greater sense of empathy and compassion towards others. They have learned to communicate more effectively and have developed a greater sense of self-awareness, which has helped them to better manage their emotions and make better decisions.
title: Transformative Sharing

text:
Section: Transformative Sharing
Overall, the VE Cell’s impact on faculty and students has been significant. The promotion of values-based education has helped to create a more positive and meaningful educational environment, which has resulted in personal transformations for many individuals. The efforts of the VE Cell have helped to foster a culture of empathy, compassion, and responsibility, which has benefitted both the individuals and society as a whole.
title: Transformative Sharing

Section: Participation in Societal Development
The VE (Value Education) Cell at AKGEC (Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College) has a mission to promote the principles and practices of value education not only within the campus but also beyond its borders. The Cell comprises a team of dedicated and self-motivated members who are well-versed in the field of value education and are capable of conducting online as well as offline Faculty and Staff Development Programs.
title: Participation in Societal Development

text:
Section: Participation in Societal Development
The members of the VE Cell are actively involved in conducting various AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education) approved FDPs (Faculty Development Programs) in different capacities. These members are experienced resource persons who are capable of delivering value-based content prescribed by AICTE.
title: Participation in Societal Development

text:
Section: Participation in Societal Development
The members of the VE Cell serve as Resource Persons, Co-facilitators, and Observers in various AICTE-approved FDPs. As Resource Persons, they are responsible for developing and delivering the sessions on value education. As Co-facilitators, they assist the lead facilitator in conducting the Universal Human Values (UHV) sessions. As Observers, they observe and evaluate the effectiveness of the UHV sessions, identify potential candidates and help resource persons and co-facilitators by giving their feedback on the sessions.
title: Participation in Societal Development

text:
Section: Participation in Societal Development
The active involvement of the members of the VE Cell in various AICTE-approved FDPs highlights their commitment to spreading the principles and practices of value education. Their dedication and inclination towards Value Education make them valuable assets to the institution and the society at large.
title: Participation in Societal Development

Section: Participation in Societal Development
Heading: 29 March 2023
The light was thrown on the importance of connection i.e having a connection with others that is based on feelings and not on the basis of our thoughts. Communication is the vital key to forming connections with those around us. Observation and Conclusion are the key points in understanding the person we are trying to communicate with. In order to show how these two work, we were shown a short role play where the students enacted out roles, and the rest of the students had to figure out and tell whether the characters were communication on the basis of observation or conclusion.

Thus, our feelings and how we act upon them are to be taken into consideration as they define our relations with others in the long run.

Heading: Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” (13-17 Jan, 2025)
The objective of the workshop was to help students recognize their innate potential to live a stable and fulfilling life. Instead of providing ready-made solutions, the facilitators encouraged students to explore their daily life challenges, helping them understand the root causes of their problems and discover their own solutions. The workshop was designed as an intense exploration process to guide students towards a better understanding of themselves and their relationships.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” (13-17 Jan, 2025)
The first day of the workshop began with an introduction to the topic and an outline of key checkpoints to be maintained throughout the sessions. The facilitator introduced students to the basic concepts of consciousness and relationships, explaining how the human consciousness often functions logically but lacks in feeling when not aligned with the right understanding. The session emphasized that recognizing one’s inherent potential and right feelings leads to a harmonious and fulfilling life. The facilitators helped students break free from preconceived notions that often lead to unhappiness. Another significant discussion revolved around expectations from others and how with the feeling can lead to a more peaceful life.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” (13-17 Jan, 2025)
From the second day onwards, the facilitator introduced students to nine fundamental feelings, starting with Trust (the foundation value) and ending with Love (the complete value). On the second day, the focus was on Trust, where the facilitator explained the difference between trust and blind trust, helping students understand how trust is ensured in relationships. The discussion then moved to Respect, where a detailed explanation of types of evaluation was provided, helping students to understand how we perceive and respect others.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” (13-17 Jan, 2025)
On the third day, the facilitator elaborated on trust in terms of intention and competence, explaining the difference between trust in intention and evaluation of competence. This helped students understand that people's intentions are right based on natural acceptance even if they lack the competence to execute them effectively. Another key discussion was the difference between Knowledge and Information, emphasizing that knowledge comes from self-exploration, while mere information does not necessarily lead to wisdom. The session also covered the feelings of guidance and affection, showing how they contribute to building strong and meaningful relationships.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” (13-17 Jan, 2025)
The fourth day focused on the next set of values: Care, Guidance, and Reverence. The facilitator explained the importance of genuinely caring for others and their well-being, the role of proper guidance in personal and professional growth, and how reverence develops acceptance for excellence for others based on their living based on right understanding. Students were encouraged to observe their surroundings and reflect on their own experiences. Their queries were resolved through self-exploration, allowing them to understand realities instead of relying solely on external influences.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” (13-17 Jan, 2025)
The final session on the last day of the workshop focused on Love, which was presented as the ultimate or complete value. Love was described as the culmination of all previous values, helping individuals achieve harmony within themselves and with others. The workshop concluded on a highly positive note, with students expressing their gratitude and appreciation for the insights gained. The feedback collected from students indicated high satisfaction, with most of them giving the workshop top ratings for its impact on their understanding of life, relationships, and self-exploration.

The workshop’s objective was to help students to see their innate potential to live a happy life. The problem today is that we fail to understand relationship and feelings (values), and consequently we fail to fulfil it despite all our good intentions. The problems are due to the absence of one or more of the right feelings (values) in the Self. And we try to make up this gap by physical facility or by trying to demand these feelings from others, rather than ensuring these feelings in ourselves and sharing it with others. The workshop was based on an intense exploration of these feelings ‘within’, where students validated the proposals in their daily life issues. The facilitators helped them to see the root cause of problems and their solutions, rather than giving any readymade solution.

Value Education Cell, AKGEC conducted an Art of Living (AoL) session on “Empowering Mental Wellness through Essential Life Skills" on 5 Oct 2023. Ms. Soma Singh and Mr. Rajeev Agarwal, Art of Living (AoL) Volunteers conducted it in an interactive manner and demonstrated SUDARSHAN KRIYA YOGA (S.K.Y.) for the participants. They stated that while breathing happens automatically, most of us are unaware that working with the breath can give us the ability to manage our minds and emotions. In fact, every emotion we experience has a corresponding rhythm in the breath. By changing the rhythms of breath, we can change our emotions. For example, the breath of peace includes a long and smooth inhale and exhale which turns into a calm and relaxed mind. Around 100 students and faculty members enthusiastically witnessed the event.

The objectives of the workshop were to equip students with the ability to express themselves fully, including their thoughts, feelings, and needs, as well as to develop their active listening skills and empathy towards others. Additionally, the workshop focused on self-counseling and communicating at a level that resonates with emotions.

Students were assigned various roles, such as brother-sister, father-son, and teacher-student, and were asked to play these roles while interacting with one another. The instructor closely observed their communication and provided valuable feedback on whether their interactions were based on feelings and whether they were able to fulfill their needs effectively.

Heading: Workshop on “Conscious Engineering” (10-18 September, 2022)
A limited hours (within 10day duration) student workshop on the topic “Conscious Engineering” was planned by the VE Cell, AKGEC, 10th September 2022 onwards, under the amiable guidance of Dr Gopal Babu, Dr Parul Verma, Prof BN Pandey, Prof RP Singh and Dr Jitendra Chhabra. The objective was to help the explorers seeing self, the conscious entity; and also the process of self-exploration. The student workshop was divided in various sessions. All the sessions were interactive; and explorers were welcomed to ask doubts, meanings, give reflections and participate actively at every point.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Conscious Engineering” (10-18 September, 2022)
The first session was started with the introduction of the topic and some checkpoints to be maintained throughout the workhop. The facilitator, Gopal ji acquainted the explorers about the basic idea of human values, how human mind tends to work logically and remains devoid of feelings in the absence of right understanding, need of Value Education and its complementarity with Skill Education and familiarization with certain terms will be used in the later sessions like self, natural acceptance, right understanding etc.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Conscious Engineering” (10-18 September, 2022)
Further session was continued understanding harmony at various levels, these are-
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Conscious Engineering” (10-18 September, 2022)
At the level of individual At the level of family At the level of society At the level of nature / existence
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Conscious Engineering” (10-18 September, 2022)
While understanding harmony at the level of individual, the proposal shared was- Human being is Co-existence of Self, a consciousness unit and the body, a material unit. The happiness of a person is dependent upon the source of imagination of the person. The sources of imagination may be preconditioning, sensation and natural acceptance. Facilitator helped explorers to find out their source of motivation for imagination.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Conscious Engineering” (10-18 September, 2022)
Then the next level of harmony was unfolded with the introduction to the nine feelings present in human beings. The nine feelings- Trust, Respect, Affection, Care, Guidance, Reverence, Glory, Gratitude and Love, were described and discussed elaborately. The foundation value Trust and the complete value Love were the ones in which the explorers had most doubts, which were been addressed very patiently by the facilitator.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

text:
Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)
Heading: Workshop on “Conscious Engineering” (10-18 September, 2022)
In the next session, the cornerstone for the level of harmony in society was laid. Correct meaning and definition of Justice was explained and various terms like Mutual Happiness and Mutual Prosperity were been elaborated. Followed by this, the levels of Nature and Existence were been explained to know the role of human being in larger. The session was insightful to understand the co-existence and live with it.
title: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

Section: Student Development Programs (SDPs)

All the explorers were divided in three groups and facilitated by a co-explorer guide to help them in understanding the right meaning of terminologies and resolving various preconditioning. The last session on weekends was planned as a special session, that is Yog Nidra. The sole purpose of the session was to provide rehabilitation to the Self. These sessions were very refreshing for everyone and every explorer gave positive feedback to these sessions.

VE Cell AKGEC conducted a 15-day workshop for female inmates of the Dasna Jail, Ghaziabad. Together, we're building a more compassionate and supportive community.

Section: Teachers Orientation Program
Heading: 8 Days Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education (22-29 June 2024)
With the vision to spread the ethos of value education, fostering individual and societal transformation through education to achieve a just and equitable society, Value Education Cell AKGEC Ghaziabad conducted an 8-day (22-29 June 2024) Teacher’s Orientation Program for the school teachers of Saraswati Vidya Mandir Rajnagar and Amrapali Global English School, Vasundhara Ghaziabad. As a great success of the previous ‘3-Day TOP’ held during 20 – 22 May 2024 at AKGEC, the 8-Day TOP requested by the principal of Saraswati Vidya Mandir was well accepted by Director General Dr R K Agarwal under the extension activity of VE Cell AKGEC. A total of 41 participants actively attended the TOP. They interacted on various issues and challenges in education in the light of proposals shared with them in a self-explorative manner. The participating teachers strongly felt the need for such holistic education that can help students realise their full human potential to ensure an equitable and just society, as expected in the new National Education Policy.
title: Teachers Orientation Program

text:
Section: Teachers Orientation Program
Heading: 8 Days Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education (22-29 June 2024)
A few teachers shared their transformative experiences of the program in the presence of the Director General, Dr R K Agarwal, Chairperson, VE Cell AKGEC, along with the chief guests, Ms Deepti Mittal, Director, Saraswati Vidya Mandir Schools, and Mr Pankaj Kumar Sharma principal, Saraswati Vidya Mandir, Rajnagar. These experiences were a testament to the program's positive impact, showing that the participants received the contents well and found them urgently needed by their school teachers and students to move towards a just and equitable society. This success story is a beacon of hope, demonstrating the potential for positive change in our education system.
title: Teachers Orientation Program

text:
Section: Teachers Orientation Program
Heading: 3 Days Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education (20-22 May 2024)
A 3-day (20-22 May 2024) Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on “The Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education- Realizing the Aspiration articulated in NEP 2020” was organised by Value Education (VE) Cell of Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, Ghaziabad. The TOP, a program of utmost importance, was an extension activity of VE Cell as Regional Nodal Centre for Value Education, AKTU, Lucknow. A total of 54 participants, including Principals, Advisors, Academic Coordinators, PGTs, TGTs and Counsellors from 12 schools in Rajasthan, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, attended the TOP with great enthusiasm and keenness, inspired by the vision of holistic value-based education. The TOP focuses on the role of education in developing human-friendly and nature-friendly mindsets in students through holistic teaching. The sessions include all aspects of human potential, like the mechanism of decision-making, health hygiene, mutually fulfilling interactions, the effort for a just and equitable society, and environmentally responsible conduct, which are aligned with the expectations stated in NEP 2020.
title: Teachers Orientation Program

text:
Section: Teachers Orientation Program
Heading: 3 Days Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education (20-22 May 2024)
Prof. Gopal Babu, Coordinator, VE Cell was the Resource Person of the TOP. He, with his team members, facilitated and smoothly conducted TOP. The Director, Dr Hemant Ahuja, and Head of VE Cell, Prof V.K. Parashar, inaugurated the session, and the Director General, Dr R.K. Agarwal, graced the closing ceremony of TOP. Shri R.P. Singh, Joint Secretary and Dr Biswajit Saha, Director, Department of Skill Education, CBSE, Ministry of Education, Government of India, New Delhi, were invited as guests in the closing ceremony. The Director General, with both the invited dignitaries, distributed certificates to all the successful participants. The Director General appreciated the team for the successful conduct of the TOP and expressed his generous intent for many more such future programs with the schools that want to be developed as a living model of values. All TOP culminated with a high tea with the participants along the Director General, Deans, HoDs and Section In-charges of the college.
